target.title: feat(google): add typed Gemini CLI auth boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The original goal is to replace OpenClaw's deprecated `google-gemini-cli` OAuth acquisition flow while keeping the Google auth replacement boundary safe and typed.

There are two supported Google/Gemini cases this PR now models separately:

- `google` API-backed profiles use Gemini API-key credentials.
- `google-gemini-cli` direct Gemini CLI profiles import OAuth credentials created by the official Gemini CLI `Sign in with Google` flow, then stage them into an isolated Gemini CLI auth home for execution.

This avoids launching an OpenClaw-owned Google OAuth browser/callback/token-exchange flow for Gemini CLI auth. OpenClaw no longer scrapes Gemini CLI OAuth client credentials or performs the deprecated `google-gemini-cli` OAuth acquisition process during provider setup.

The PR still keeps the public CLI backend auth-forwarding contract generic, preserves Gemini CLI API-key staging, and makes provider-owned hooks fail closed when they decline forwarding.

## What Changed

- Added official Gemini CLI OAuth cache import support for `google-gemini-cli` setup.
- Changed `google-gemini-cli` setup to import the official Gemini CLI `oauth_creds.json` cache instead of starting OpenClaw's own Google OAuth flow.
- Added provider-level coverage proving setup imports the official Gemini CLI cache and does not open/log/prompt for an OpenClaw-owned OAuth callback flow.
- Added low-level cache import coverage for `GEMINI_CLI_HOME/.gemini/oauth_creds.json`, active Google account import, and project binding from `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` / `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID`.
- Added a public provider hook, `resolveCliBackendAuthCredential`, for provider-owned CLI backend credential resolution.
- Added generic fallback forwarding for standard auth-profile credentials only when the selected provider has no provider-owned hook.
- Made hook absence distinct from hook decline: a registered hook returning `null` or `undefined` blocks forwarding instead of falling through to generic fallback.
- Registered the Gemini CLI OAuth resolver on the bundled `google-gemini-cli` provider.
- Preserved Google API-key fallback forwarding for `google` API-key profiles and Gemini CLI `GEMINI_API_KEY` staging.
- Preserved backend allowlist checks before and after credential resolution.
- Fixed CLI runner cleanup gaps on mid-prepare failures.
- Made bundled MCP fail closed when loopback startup fails instead of writing a partial config.
- Removed the unused core Google auth resolver and its self-only test; credential resolution now remains provider-owned plus the generic fallback path.
- Updated Google provider docs and docs map so fresh Gemini CLI setup requires official Gemini CLI `Sign in with Google` first and explicitly retires the OpenClaw-owned OAuth client env-var setup path.
- Updated Plugin SDK exports/API baseline and CLI backend plugin docs.
- Updated the proof script so it installs the real Google provider/backend registry, verifies the registered provider hook through runtime lookup, verifies official Gemini CLI cache import, verifies provider setup does not use OpenClaw-owned OAuth, runs `prepareCliRunContext`, and executes the staged Gemini CLI auth-home writes.
- Removed a proof-local SHA-256 recomputation that CodeQL misclassified as a weak password hash; the proof now asserts against `resolveGeminiCliProfileHome(...)` directly.

## Evidence

Validated locally through PR head `f09554cafa765453a410b58c4a7fcb3fee8649b9` after merging current `main`.

```text
pnpm check:test-types
```

Result: passed.

```text
OPENCLAW_DOCS_SYNC_CLAWHUB_REPO="$PWD/clawhub-source" pnpm check:docs
```

Result: passed.

```text
pnpm test extensions/google/oauth.test.ts extensions/google/index.test.ts extensions/google/index-harness-registration.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts
```

Result: 2 Vitest shards passed, 106 tests passed.

```text
pnpm tsx scripts/proof-google-auth-replacement.ts
```

Result: passed. The proof output included:

```json
{
  "registeredGeminiCliProviderHook": true,
  "googleApiKeyProviderUsesGenericFallback": true,
  "cliRunnerForwardedOauthViaRegisteredProviderHook": true,
  "cliRunnerForwardedApiKeyViaGenericFallback": true,
  "apiKeyProfileSelectedForGoogle": true,
  "oauthProfileSelectedForGeminiCli": true,
  "geminiCliOfficialOAuthCacheImported": true,
  "geminiCliOfficialOAuthAccountImported": true,
  "geminiCliOfficialOAuthProjectImported": true,
  "geminiCliProviderSetupImportsOfficialCache": true,
  "geminiCliProviderSetupDoesNotUseOpenClawOAuth": true,
  "geminiCliUsesIsolatedAuthHome": true,
  "inheritedGoogleAuthEnvCleared": true,
  "apiKeyNotWrittenIntoGeminiCliOAuthFiles": true,
  "apiKeyProfileStagesGeminiApiKey": true,
  "apiKeyProfileDoesNotLeaveOauthFiles": true,
  "oauthTokenValuesRedactedFromProofOutput": true,
  "profileHomeUsesResolverDerivedPath": true,
  "rawProfileIdAbsentFromHome": true,
  "selectedCredentialKinds": {
    "google-gemini-cli": "oauth",
    "google": "api_key"
  }
}
```


```text

```

Result: 3 Vitest shards passed, 140 tests passed at the earlier head before the unused resolver/test cleanup.

## Owner Acceptance

Provider owner acceptance: pending.

Plugin SDK owner acceptance: pending.

Security owner acceptance: pending.

## What Was Not Tested

I did not perform a live Google account login. The replacement intentionally imports the official Gemini CLI cache created by the official Gemini CLI login flow, and the deterministic proof exercises that cache import path in-process.

I did not run a live Gemini CLI subprocess against Google's service. The deterministic proof exercises provider setup, official cache import, provider hook resolution, CLI runner preparation, forwarding allowlists, isolated auth-home staging, env clearing, API-key staging, redaction, SDK baseline, docs checks, test-type checks, and focused regression coverage in-process.

I did not run the full repository test suite; the focused suite covers the changed Google auth boundary, official Gemini CLI cache import, Gemini staging, CLI preparation, SDK export, provider registration, docs, type checks, and proof behavior.

## Tests

AI-assisted: yes.

## Real behavior proof

Latest proof file: `/home/rev/pr-98343-antigravity-real-behavior-proof.txt`

Antigravity OAuth provider proof for commit `30e5b743ac`:

- Verified pushed PR head matches local HEAD: `30e5b743acbf3baf60815be302e337227a30590a`.
- Verified installed Antigravity binary: `/usr/bin/antigravity`.
- Verified installed Antigravity version: `1.107.0`.
- Verified `antigravity chat --help` is app/window-session oriented and does not expose a proven stdout/headless runtime surface.
- Verified the installed Antigravity extension declares the `antigravity_auth` authentication provider plus login/auth-token commands.
- Verified OpenClaw registers `google-antigravity` as an OAuth/session setup provider.
- Verified OpenClaw does not register a `google-antigravity` CLI backend and does not reference `antigravity chat` as a runtime command.
- Verified the provider does not write a default model, config patch, or agent runtime config while no non-GUI Antigravity runtime API is proven.
- Verified focused Google provider tests pass: `pnpm test extensions/google/index-harness-registration.test.ts extensions/google/setup-api.test.ts`.
- Verified SDK checks pass: `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` and `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`.
- Verified diff hygiene with `git diff --check`.
